taxonomyNote: NatureServe's L. getula is the eastern kingsnake (Krysko et al. 2017 split the former common kingsnake into several species); neither source read uses the name 'black kingsnake'. Animal Diversity Web treats L. getula broadly as the 'common kingsnake' with seven subspecies.
fieldMarks: Eastern kingsnake adults 61-153 cm: large, solid, glossy black with yellow (sometimes white) crossbars.
Head solid black with yellow or white spots on head scales.
Speckled kingsnake (L. g. holbrooki) is black with yellow specks on the scales, belly pale yellow to white.
behavior: Diurnal; active late March-early April to October-early November and hibernates in crevices, burrows, hollow logs and stumps; in hot weather may be active at night.
Spends about 79% of time under cover; climbs and swims well.
Eats mainly other snakes, including venomous species, plus lizards, small turtles, reptile eggs, frogs, birds and small mammals.
habitat: Wide range of habitats, often in or near woods and near water; cover includes wood, trash piles, barns and stone walls.
range: Eastern West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware and southern New Jersey south through the southeastern United States to southern Alabama.
